headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; no direct pairwise docs, so uncertainty is elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads/writes repo files and can use MCP; firecrawl exposes MCP-compatible client support and broad API-driven content ingestion. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled web content from firecrawl can reach Claude Code through files or MCP, even though direct pairwise docs are absent. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is written into a shared repo file or MCP message consumed by Claude Code, injection is plausible.
IF Claude Code parses firecrawl-sourced text as instructions without provenance checks, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of firecrawl output into Claude Code prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to all firecrawl-derived text before handoff.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Require manual review before Claude Code acts on scraped content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while firecrawl handles web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive local data can be copied into firecrawl requests or outputs. The pairwise path is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or files, local secrets can flow from Claude Code into firecrawl inputs.
IF firecrawl is asked to scrape or upload content derived from Claude Code's workspace, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials for each agent.
Redact secrets before any firecrawl handoff.
Restrict firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive URLs.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after shared-workspace use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret-scanning at the orchestration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support and broad egress. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes or git mutations can overwrite each other. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF firecrawl writes artifacts into the same repo Claude Code edits, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents mutate git state without an external lock, commits or branches can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Make firecrawl output read-only until reviewed.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or facts from files and git history, and firecrawl can ingest web content and structured data. If firecrawl output is treated as authoritative by Claude Code, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or downstream actions. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is fed directly into Claude Code prompts, Claude Code may act on unverified content.
IF Claude Code uses scraped data as facts for edits or commits, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before acting on scraped data.
Tag firecrawl outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Compare scraped facts against a second source before edits.
Limit Claude Code to draft-only changes from firecrawl input.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between scrape and action.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state residency, certifications, or retention mismatches. Claude Code explicitly handles local source code and git history; firecrawl handles web content and API keys. With no documented compliance mismatch, only a low residual risk remains, and the other agent is not separately cited because no cross-border or policy gap is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent without a matching policy, compliance risk increases.
IF firecrawl is used on data subject to stricter retention or residency rules than Claude Code's workspace, a mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Document retention for both tools.
Keep jurisdiction-sensitive data out of firecrawl jobs.
Review vendor policies before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
